summary: All three generated images were opened at original resolution. The global six-view image is unclipped and clearly shows the complete bent sheet-metal part, but contains no ribbon overlay despite broad visible folds and transitions. The ARC_SPAN_LOW control shows a compact, spatially coherent near-miss at the right-hand end with a smooth pole-aligned preimage and Gauss-band distances approaching the 12-degree boundary; its insufficient-span rejection is plausible but the image does not expose the exact span statistic. The ANGULAR_DISCONNECTION control visibly shows a curved source fragment whose projective-angle samples occupy separated groups, supporting that rejection. Two later-stage controls (longitudinal occupancy and ruling coherence) are NOT_PRESENT because no component reached them; no permuted overlay or causal-control image exists because zero ribbons survived. Therefore the scalar zero-ribbon result is deterministic and internally consistent but visually indicates an overselective or underexpressive frozen representation, not an absence of bend-like geometry. The architecture STOP is supportable for this frozen PGRR specification, while visual_audit_ok must remain false because the complete required visual ladder was not constructible and the aggregate zero hides coherent near-misses.
